name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jasmine Clark has large financial and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
model.rationale: The district's D+21 lean makes this a heavily Democratic seat, and Clark's $1.6 million raised plus $4.2 million in outside support against a Republican with no reported fundraising reinforces that advantage. Markets price a Democratic win around 97%, consistent with a Safe D call.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower race or unexpected Republican outside spending would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Atlanta-area House seat is one of Georgia's most Democratic districts, with a partisan lean of D+21. David Scott's retirement and Everton Blair's absence from the ballot leave an open seat, but the underlying partisanship still strongly favors the Democratic nominee, Jasmine Clark.

Clark has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $4.2 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez reports no significant fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97%. The forecast calls the race Safe Democratic with an expected margin near 25 points.
